knowledge_point.title: Calculating Indefinite Integrals Using Substitution with Inverse Tangent

question.:question/worked-solution:
This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse tangent,

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\text{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have $2{x}^{2}=(\sqrt{2}x)^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=\sqrt{2}x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\sqrt{2}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{18}{1+2{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =18\int \frac{1}{1+(\sqrt{2}x)^{2}}\text{d}x \\  & =18\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\cdot (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{18}{\sqrt{2}}\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{18\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C \\  & =9\sqrt{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{2}x)+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{19}{36+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{19}{36\cdot (1+{x}^{2}/36)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{19}{36}\int \frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}/36}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{19}{36}\int \frac{1}{1+(x/6)^{2}}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse tangent

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\text{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have ${(\frac{x}{6})}^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{x}{6}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{6}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=6\,\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{19}{36+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{19}{36}\int \frac{1}{1+(x/6)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{19}{36}\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\cdot (6\,\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{19}{6}\int \frac{\text{d}u}{1+{u}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{19}{6}\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{19}{6}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{6})+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
